title: Baseball API — Background Jobs
description: Media import pipeline and MLBAM/Fangraphs reference-update jobs: are they running, succeeding, and keeping the data matched? Source of truth: docs/observability/dashboards/ in the repo.

options.content:
Every background job emits a `job.*` span per run; the run/error/duration panels are built from Grafana's server-side span metrics, which only cover SERVER and CONSUMER spans — the job spans are deliberately emitted as CONSUMER (`Telemetry.StartJob`) so they show up here. Data starts when that change is deployed; runs before it (Internal spans) are visible in Tempo but absent from these three panels. Expected cadence — `job.media-import`: on demand · `job.update-team-references`: 12h · `job.update-player-references`: 24h · `job.update-fangraphs-links`: 6h · `job.set-content-types`: 12h · `job.create-alternate-formats`: 1h · `job.cleanse-temp-files`: 12h · `job.cleanse-abandoned-files`: 24h · `job.retrigger-imports`: 1h · `job.upload-logs`: 1h · `job.cleanup-old-logs`: 24h. A job missing from "runs" for ~2× its cadence is a problem even if nothing is red.

**To investigate a failed run:** Explore → Tempo → TraceQL: `{name =~ "job\\..*" && status = error}` — the trace shows every DB query and outbound HTTP call the job made, with the exception on the failing span.

panels.title: Job runs (dashboard time range)
panels.description: How many times each job ran in the selected window. Compare against the cadence in the header — a missing job is as bad as a failing one.

panels.title: Job failures (dashboard time range)
panels.description: Runs that ended with an error status on the job span. Anything nonzero deserves a look — use the TraceQL query in the header to find the failing trace. Note: cancellations at shutdown are deliberately NOT counted as failures.

panels.title: Job duration p95
panels.description: How long each job takes. Media imports are legitimately hours-long for video batches; the interesting signal is a job whose duration suddenly changes shape.

panels.title: Media import outcomes (per hour)
panels.description: Final outcome of each import run. CAVEAT: 'skipped' is mostly benign noise — the hourly retrigger job re-queues anything still Queued/InProgress, and each duplicate pop lands here as 'skipped' once the real run finishes. Watch 'failed'; ignore a steady trickle of 'skipped' during long imports.

panels.title: Media import queue depth
panels.description: Tasks waiting in the in-memory queue. CAVEAT: this counts queue ENTRIES, not remaining work — the hourly retrigger re-adds the currently-running task, so a single multi-hour import shows a +1-per-hour staircase that drains all at once on completion. Read it as 'is there work pending?' (>0), not as a backlog size. It also resets to 0 on every deploy (the retrigger repopulates it within the hour).

panels.title: Tracked Players: matched to MLB reference data
panels.description: All Players in the DB, split by whether they link to a ReferencePlayer, as of the last daily reference run. Unmatched is EXPECTED to be large (the MLBAM feed is current-season MLB only; MiLB and historical players can't match). The signal is the trend: matched should creep up, and a sudden drop means the matcher broke. Uses last_over_time because the gauge is silent from each deploy until the next run (~30+ min).

panels.title: Actionable match problems
panels.description: Ambiguous name groups: distinct names shared by multiple tracked Players that the last run couldn't uniquely match. Fixable players: the unmatched Players inside those groups — every one can be resolved by setting a date of birth. The specific names are in the run's logs: search for 'Ambiguous match' below or in Explore.

panels.title: MLBAM feed match outcomes (per daily run)
panels.description: Disposition of each of the ~1,200 feed players in the daily run, summed over 25h so each point covers exactly one run. Stable proportions are healthy; a spike in 'ambiguous' or collapse of 'linked_*' means matching regressed (e.g. a name-normalization change).

panels.title: Job errors and ambiguous-match warnings
panels.description: Warning+ log lines from the background jobs, including the per-name 'Ambiguous match' details that the stat panel counts.
